Skip next section President calls for end to fear after Berlin Pride attack 08/15/2026 August 15, 2026 President calls for end to fear after Berlin Pride attack The motto for Darmstaft Pride was: Show yourself for all of us Image: Peter Henrich/HEN-FOTO/IMAGO German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has urged society to protect the LGBTQ+ community against attacks like the van ramming and stabbing near the Berlin Pride parade three weeks ago. On July 25, an Islamist attacker drove a van into a crowd and then allegedly attacked people with a machete, killing a woman and injuring at least 31 people. "In an open society, everyone must be able to follow their own path," Steinmeier wrote in an article for the Zeit Online website. This right applies "not only without fear, but also with pride; not only in private, but also in public," he asserted. "Everyone has the right to self-determination, particularly where it concerns the very core of every human being — the expression of one's own personality, love and partnership, physicality and sexuality," the head of state continued. Steinmeier said the attack primarily targeted queer people, leaving many afraid. He stressed that a robust democracy cannot tolerate this and must prioritize law enforcement, public safety and education. The head of state made the comments as several smaller German cities held their own Pride events this weekend, including Darmstadt, Bayreuth, Krefeld and Münster. https://p.dw.com/p/5ItUR Skip next section Berlin's Rave the Planet techno event starts with moment of silence 08/15/2026 August 15, 2026 Berlin's Rave the Planet techno event starts with moment of silence As tens of thousands of partiers gathered for "Rave the Planet" — a Berlin music event labeling itself a political demonstration — there was quiet before organizers began blasting music. The now high-security event began with a moment of silence for the victims of an Islamist attack on an LGBTQ+ pride event at the same spot three weeks ago. Taking place under the motto "imagine love," Rave the Planet is the first major party event in the German capital since the July 25 terror attack. A Christopher Street Day (CSD) organizer invited to Saturday's event called on those gathered to "be courageous" … "especially now." A large police presence is on hand to protect revelers, streets and paths have been closed and trams will not stop at regular destinations as a result of the event. Security was heightened and movement in the city limited as a result of saturday's techno event Image: Volodymyr Sindieiev/picture alliance https://p.dw.com/p/5It8v Skip next section Rhine water levels fall again 08/15/2026 August 15, 2026 Rhine water levels fall again The Rhine, seen here in Bingen, is a trickle of its former self Image: Arnulf Hettrich/imageBROKER/picture alliance Water levels on the Rhine River have fallen to new record lows , greatly disrupting river-borne cargo transport, as a prolonged dry spell continues in most of Germany. According to the inland navigation agency WSV, the water level gauge at the Kaub bottleneck near Koblenz fell to 6 centimeters (2.4 inches) late on Friday and was 8 cm ​early on Saturday. Until this year, the previous lowest level marked by the gauge was 25 cm recorded ‌in 2018. The gauge gives the depth over an arbitrary baseline near the bank of the river, but is an indication of the navigable depth at that point, which is around a meter (3 feet) deeper. Most cargo previously transported on the Rhine has been shifted to road and rail, but these transport methods cannot fully compensate for the heavy loads carried by ships. For this reason, companies have ​started to report disruption to their supplies , with c hemical producers, utilities, steelmakers warning of higher costs, transport bottlenecks and reduced production. When high concentrations occur in water, the algae can cause allergic reactions and irritation to skin and mucous membranes, and nausea and vomiting if ingested in sufficient quantities. Satellite images from the Federal Maritime and Hydrographic Agency show large patches of the algae — which are, in fact, cyanobacteria — in the Baltic Sea off the coast between Rostock and Hiddensee island, extending across the sea to the Danish coast. They have also been found in lakes in the state of Schleswig-Holstein . Swimming in them has been banned until, probably, Wednesday. The incident in the city of Stendal occurred just weeks before an election in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The Spiegel cited the State Criminal Police Office (LKA) as saying that the boy, along with other youths, was caught in the act of damaging an AfD poster. "Subsequently, there was a possible physical altercation between a person with immunity and the youths. In the course of this, a blunt instrument was allegedly used," the LKA is quoted as saying. It said one of the youths was slightly injured and received medical treatment. Spiegel cited sources close to the boy as saying he suffered slight concussion, several bruises and injuries to his lip. The public-service broadcaster MDR said the "blunt instrument" concerned was a baseball bat. https://p.dw.com/p/5Irw5 Skip next section Heightened security planned at Berlin techno parade 08/15/2026 August 15, 2026 Heightened security planned at Berlin techno parade The Techno Parade, some of whose participants are seen here in 2023, is a major spectacle Image: Christoph Soeder/dpa/picture alliance The techno parade Rave the Planet is expected to draw tens of thousands of people in Berlin in Saturday, with police stepping up security at the event after last month's Islamist attack on fringes of the Pride march in the capital. Participants in the parade will also have to contend with high temperatures of up to 37 C (98.6 F). Police say they will deploy at least one water cannon to spray a cooling water mist and free drinking water is to be made available along the route of the parade, organizers have said. The parade is to start in the early afternoon and run until late in the evening. It is planned to run along the main boulevard through the Tiergarten park, between the Brandenburg Gate and the Victory Column, close to the site of the July 25 attack, in which an Islamist assailant killed a woman and injured at least 31 people, some seriously. A police spokeswoman said some 1,500 officers would be deployed at the event, with Berlin police supported by colleagues from the states of Brandenburg and Saxony-Anhalt. The techno parade was first held in Berlin in 2022 to celebrate electronic music culture and has taken place every year since then. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck1e.text: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea By Koh Ewe Â and Â Julianna Khan Published 15 October 2026, 03:59 BST Updated 07:24 BST A long-delayed road bridge linking China and North Korea has opened, Chinese state media report, as trade ties improve between the neighbours. China is North Korea's largest trading partner and a lifeline against heavy international sanctions over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme. The New Yalu River Bridge spans 3km (1.9 miles) from the Chinese border city of Dandong to Sinuiju in North Korea, and is set to become the main land route for trade between them. Its launch, initially slated for 2014, had been indefinitely postponed after North Korea halted construction of its roads and customs facilities, as relations with Beijing turned frosty. Chinese Premier Li Qiang, in a video address on Thursday, said the bridge was a "new landmark symbolising the traditional friendship between China and North Korea", and that the two countries were "opening a new chapter" in bilateral ties. The New Yalu River Bridge is an alternative to the decades-old Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which was built between 1937 and 1943 during Imperial Japan's occupation of the region. The new bridge is an "important facility for connectivity" between the two countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Wednesday, adding that the route would "further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges". Last year, bilateral trade reached $2.7bn, marking a recovery to pre-pandemic levels, mostly fuelled by Chinese exports to North Korea. A sharp and sudden increase in trade across the border is "unlikely" as the UN sanctions on North Korea remain in effect, Kang Jun-young, a professor of Chinese studies at the Hankuk University of Foreign Studies, tells the BBC. "Pyongyang is also wary of a sudden flood of Chinese imports that would greatly expand China's influence over its domestic market," he adds. "China is well aware of these concerns, so trade is more likely to grow gradually." Beijing and Pyongyang are long-standing allies with a mutual defence treaty, the only one that China has with any country. The relationship is often described "as close as lips and teeth", a remark first made by China's former leader Mao Zedong. Figure caption, Watch: Why did Xi Jinping visit North Korea? But the alliance is not without tension. Ties were frosty for much of the 2010s as Beijing's patience over Pyongyang's nuclear weapons programme wore thin. Kim Jong Un conducted a nuclear test in 2017 and has since ramped up tests of banned ballistic missiles - all of which increased US wariness, and strengthened its military alliances with South Korea and Japan. China's attitude has shifted more recently. "Whilst only a decade ago, Beijing was overtly critical of North Korea's nuclearisation - and indeed calling for Pyongyang's denuclearisation - China is now saying little, if anything, to this effect," Edward Howell, a lecturer at the University of Oxford, tells the BBC. Observers say one reason is that North Korea has grown closer to Russia because of the Ukraine war. At least 2,300 North Korean soldiers are believed to have died fighting for Russia in Ukraine. In return, Russia supplies North Korea with oil, in violation of UN sanctions. In 2024, Russia was estimated to have sent more than a billion barrels of oil as payment for Pyongyang's weapons and troops. Last month, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge, which Russian state media said would allow the movement of up to 300 vehicles and more than 2,000 people every day. So Beijing is believed to be trying to reassert its sway over Pyongyang by rekindling ties. Air China resumed direct flights between Beijing and Pyongyang in March after a six-year hiatus triggered by the pandemic. The two countries reopened passenger train services the same month. Chinese President Xi Jinping's first state visit of this year, in June, was to Pyongyang, where he met North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. "The opening of the New Yalu River Bridge demonstrates bilateral relations are improving and that Xi Jinping's June visit to North Korea was more than symbolic," says Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul. "But the long delay, including North Korea's pandemic self-isolation and domestic socioeconomic crackdowns, shows what a difficult partner Pyongyang can be for Beijing."
